prompt: You want to add dark window tint and colored accent lights to your car. What should you know before you install them?
choices: Anything sold at an auto parts store is legal to put on a car
Equipment laws cover only what the factory installed, not add-ons
They can be illegal if they don't meet your state's equipment laws
Tint and lighting rules apply only to trucks and commercial vehicles
explanation: Aftermarket changes such as window tint and extra lights must meet legal standards, like limits on how dark tint can be and which light colors are allowed. A store selling a product does not make it legal on the road, so check your state's rules first.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. CT p.14, MA p.42, MN p.27, IA p.24)

prompt: You are following a pickup truck on a gravel road. How should your following distance compare with what you use on dry pavement?
choices: Keep the same gap, since gravel roads usually have lower speed limits
Stay closer, so the truck's dust cloud doesn't hide the road ahead
Leave a shorter gap, since loose gravel slows cars down faster
Leave more room, since you need longer to stop on loose gravel
explanation: Gravel and dirt give your tires much less grip than concrete or asphalt, so stopping takes longer and skids start more easily. Slow down and increase your following distance; hanging back also keeps you out of the dust the vehicle ahead kicks up.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. KS p.90, LA p.108, NJ p.98)

prompt: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: The right lane ends, so drivers in it must merge left
Traffic from a ramp will merge into your lane from the right
A new lane opens on the right for slower traffic
The road narrows, and both directions share one lane
explanation: This symbol sign means the right lane is ending. If you are in it, find a safe gap and merge left; if you are in the lane next to it, adjust your speed so merging drivers can get in.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2C; state driver handbooks (e.g. IN p.34, CA p.43, FL p.57)

prompt: Why can a state suspend or take away your driver's license when you break traffic laws?
choices: Driving is a right that can be limited only for drivers under 21
Licenses belong to the car's owner, not to the driver
Driving is a privilege, not a right
A license is a contract that only a judge can end
explanation: A driver's license is a privilege that you earn and keep by obeying the law, not a right. If you break traffic laws or drive impaired, the state can suspend or revoke it.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. KS p.14, FL p.31, PA p.3)

prompt: You are about to slow down and stop at the side of the road. What should you check first?
choices: Your mirrors, for traffic behind you
Your speedometer, to know your exact speed
Your fuel gauge, before you shut off the engine
Your parking brake, so it is ready to set
explanation: Check your mirrors whenever you slow down or stop, especially when you slow quickly or where drivers behind you would not expect it, such as at a driveway or parking space. Then signal so they know what you plan to do.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. KS p.58, CT p.24, MT p.64, NM p.20)
